headline_marked: [[Ronaldo, Modric break World Cup records]] in Portugal-Croatia clash, honouring Jota
headline: Ronaldo, Modric break World Cup records in Portugal-Croatia clash, honouring Jota
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo and Luka Modric achieve new World Cup milestones as Portugal faces Croatia in a Round of 32 match, coinciding with the first death anniversary of Portuguese forward Diogo Jota.
details: Ronaldo (41y, 147d) became the oldest outfield player to start a World Cup knockout match for Portugal against Croatia in Toronto. Croatia captain Luka Modric (40y, 296d) moved into second place, both surpassing Edin Dzeko's recent record.

This match also marks Ronaldo's 26th World Cup appearance, moving him past Lothar Matthaeus into second all-time behind Lionel Messi. He is also making his sixth World Cup appearance, a milestone shared by Messi and Guillermo Ochoa.

Ronaldo had previously become the first player to score in six different World Cup editions, netting twice against Uzbekistan. This brace also made him Portugal's leading World Cup scorer with 10 goals, surpassing Eusebio.

The Round of 32 clash carries deep emotional weight as it coincides with the first death anniversary of Portuguese forward Diogo Jota. Jota, 28, and his brother Andre Silva were killed in a car crash in Spain a year ago.

Portugal players are wearing wristbands bearing Jota's name, presented by Prime Minister Luis Montenegro, vowing to wear them throughout the tournament. Close friend Ruben Neves, who inherited Jota's number 21 shirt, has led tributes.

Portugal made one change to their lineup, with Rafael Leao replacing Joao Felix. Croatia maintained an unchanged squad. The winner of this first-ever World Cup meeting between the two nations will face Spain in Dallas for a quarterfinal spot.
Ronaldo aims for another personal milestone, having never scored in a World Cup knockout match. Portugal hopes to honor Jota's memory with a victory.
